bluf: Rise, formerly Rise Interactive, is Quad's Chicago integrated media agency: enterprise media buying across programmatic, CTV, paid social and retail media, sold on measurement and audience intelligence. It rebranded in 2024-03, won Gorilla Glue as media agency of record in 2026-02, and its insights feed carries a 2026 AdExchanger Awards finalist post dated 2026-09-28. What a rival should know: Horus reads it at minus 9.1, most exposed to KJ6 at net 0.675 against, with no public pricing model, and its own house shows 0 Google ads and 0 LinkedIn ads.
doing:
The positioning line, "Quad's integrated media agency: data-driven omnichannel media buying tied to measurement, customer insights and audience intelligence," decodes to a holdco media buyer that sells the analytics behind the buy. The headline claim is borrowed authority: per parent Quad's newsroom, Rise appears in a Forrester 2026 analyst report on media management service providers, and Quad itself made the Ad Age Agency Report 2026 and, in June 2026, the MM+M Agency 100.

The sold mix leads with Data & Measurement and Programmatic & CTV, both scored 3 by the capability read: analytics platform enablement, customer insights, audience intelligence and measurement services, plus Connex, a cross channel insights tool known only from a URL slug; programmatic and connected TV were listed as services at the relaunch. Paid Social (Atkins registrations, Ulta Snapchat Lenses) and Retail Media (Amazon Ads services, a Tempur Sealy Amazon profitability case) score 2. The only partner listed is an impact.com directory listing, and a 2025-02-21 case study names a Rise Affiliate Network. The read scores Paid Search 0, yet dated case studies describe Performance Max for eye exam bookings (2025-03-30), Microsoft PMax and Audience ads for America's Best (2026-01-19) and AI fueled Google campaigns for DMI (2025-09-24), so search is very likely understated in the read.

The record gives no AI posture. AI Search / GEO and AI Automation / Agents score 0; AI shows up only as platform automation inside client work and in an insights post on conversational AI dated 2026-09-15.

In date order: the rebrand from Rise Interactive in 2024-03; Gorilla Glue named it media agency of record in 2026-02, consolidating media and creative under Quad; an insights post on being a 2026 AdExchanger Awards finalist is dated 2026-09-28. The record lists no pricing, no jobs, no founding year and no headcount.
clients:
The record types the client base as enterprise and lists Beauty & cosmetics, Consumer packaged goods, Home furnishings, Footwear & apparel and Home improvement & DIY, with its only listed office in Chicago, so the home market is the US. The dated case studies add healthcare, which the list omits: messaging and hyper local work for a children's hospital (2025-03-01, 2025-02-25) and NorthShore University (2025-02-28), alongside Stanley Steemer (2026-01-02), America's Best (2026-01-19), DMI and AEB, none of them counted by the needs read.

Five clients are named: three observed and two names only. Tempur Sealy came for commerce and marketplaces, the slug reading "scaling amazon performance while improving profitability"; Atkins for social and creators, "increasing registrations through social"; ColourPop for B2B pipeline on the signal "premium linkedin". All three sit on undated riseinteractive.com pages from before the rebrand. Gorilla Glue is coded names only, although its 2026-02 press release names Rise media agency of record, which reads as a paid media need. Ulta Beauty is coded names only too, yet dated case studies on the new site name it for Snapchat AR lenses (2025-03-19), the Rise Affiliate Network (2025-02-21) and seasonal campaigns (2025-02-27). Atkins also sits on the digitas book and Ulta Beauty on the billion-dollar-boy book: the two shared clients, both accounts that buy from more than one agency.

Under KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), these consumer brands will likely press a holdco agency on fees and outputs (moderate confidence). Under KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), they will likely need the first party data and measurement inputs that platform automation runs on, the line Rise leads with (moderate confidence).
house: The house record is close to blank. Its Transparency Center record shows 0 Google ads, and 0 LinkedIn ads match the name query across all advertisers. Both say and do tests are unknown rather than failed: Paid Social because no pixel was detected and the gap scan did not flag it, LinkedIn advertising because the Ad Library lookup returned none. The compile captured no sitemap counts, tags, CMS, pixels, llms.txt result or social links, and no AI crawler is listed as blocked; with nothing resolved, Horus gives no house integrity score and the Radar flagged no gaps. openings:
The strongest opening is pricing. Rise is most exposed to KJ6 at net 0.675 against and publishes no pricing model (P5 unknown), so a rival offering outcome priced media with first party measurement is likely to win enterprise consumer brands reviewing holdco fees (moderate confidence). Falsifier: a published pricing or outcome fee model from Rise or Quad at the next compile.

Second, the AI layer is unclaimed: no AI posture, AI Search / GEO at 0, P1 absent and feed work only partial (P2). For beauty and packaged goods clients facing agentic checkout under KJ4, a rival with AI shopping visibility and feed work likely has an open door (low confidence). Third, Atkins and Ulta Beauty buy from more than one tracked agency (digitas, billion-dollar-boy), a roughly even chance to be contestable, while Gorilla Glue, consolidated under Quad in 2026-02, is very unlikely to move soon. A rival should not read the Paid Search 0 as weakness: the case studies show Performance Max and Microsoft PMax work. A pure price attack is unlikely to land: displacement reads 36.8.
